liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (5 reviews): The reviewer points to the peak of the jam where the band returns to the lyrics as sizzling; The ending of Viola Lee Blues is intact on The Golden Road box set and the 2003 reissue of the first album [6][8][13][14][15]
- **In the Midnight Hour** (4 reviews): The roughly 31-minute jam has dreamy, psychedelic improvisation around minutes 12 to 14, with inspired raps from Pigpen; Midnight Hour runs about 31 minutes, with Pigpen impressive throughout [5][10][12][13]
- **Dancing In The Street** (2 reviews): Jerry sounds already transcendent on Dancing In The Streets, and again on Midnight Hour; Weir is rhythmically lost on Dancing, which the reviewer calls a sonic disaster despite Pigpen and Jerry's efforts [14][15]
- **Alligator** (1 review, 1 other source): Alligator is also singled out as outstanding; Alligator has no Caution yet; it just returns to the shouted Alligator refrain and ends [2][15]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Cold Rain and Snow is described as ripping, with a hot, energetic performance [6]

## The recordings

- **gd67-09-03.sbd.backus.17272.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 8 songs; 102 min; rated 4.62/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: The long jam's audio is hissy and degraded, though still listenable and enjoyable; The mix takes several minutes to settle, Viola Lee is cut at both ends, and Alligator's sound deteriorates late [1][5]
- **gd1967-09-03.sbd.miller.43.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 71 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Schoolgirl is cut at 10:43, Viola Lee is cut at both ends, and the opening mix takes minutes to come together [2]
- **gd1967-09-03.sbd.oconnell-clevenger.6180.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 71 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: The mix takes several minutes to come together, Viola Lee is cut at both ends, and Alligator's sound deteriorates [3]

## Around the show

- The reviewer claims to have driven Jerry to the Dance Hall, and says they asked him for a killer Midnight Hour [9]
- The crowd was reportedly only about 25 people at a Russian River resort over Labor Day weekend 1967 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-09-03.sbd.backus.17272.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jon Miller; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The jam was officially released on Phil Lesh's Fallout from the Phil Zone, but the reviewer is glad the tape is still free; First-generation tape, not a master; lineage is silver CD bootleg to EAC to SHN via MKWACT; Midnight Hour was added to this seed by terrapinstation in April 2002, and its placement in the show is uncertain [1][5]
- **gd1967-09-03.sbd.miller.43.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jon Miller; source: RM > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [2]. Also: Encoded by T. OConnell; the info file comes from the BUDD vine, and Midnight Hour is missing from this version [2]
- **gd1967-09-03.sbd.oconnell-clevenger.6180.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sbd [3]. Also: First-generation tape, not a master, uploaded by Jon Miller and originally from a BUDD SHN vine [3]
- Source chain listed as RM, then C, then DAT, CD, EAC and SHN [17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [Grateful Dead Poster 1967-09-03 - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/grateful-dead-poster-1967-09-03-03/) [22]
